section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The CompressJPEG module has been extended beyond the functions provided by the original version as documented in PRM 5a-609. In particular it is now possible to transcode JPEGs (convert from one form of JPEG to another without loss of information), to add comments and to create JPEGs from arbitrary paletted data.

swi-definition.name: CompressJPEG_WriteLineExtended
swi-definition.description: Write lines to a JPEG from a generic source

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Pixel type, size of pixels (number of colours):
1bit (2 colours, palette supplied in R3) 2bits (4 colours, palette supplied in R3) 4bits (16 colours, palette supplied in R3) 8bits (256 colours, palette supplied in R3) 16bits (32767 colours, 15bits of colour data) 32bits (16M colours, 24bits of colour data) Reserved 24bits (16M colour, flag bits 4 and 5 are ignored)
Palette has double entries (flashing colours included) If set, colour data has any spare data in high bits If set, colour data holds the red component in the high bits; if clear, colour data holds the red component in the low bits Reserved
Pointer to palette data (for pixel type 0-3)
Bytes between each line (for alignment issues)

exit.register-use: Number of lines that were not written

use.p: This SWI can be used to write a line to a JPEG from a more generic source than with CompressJPEG_WriteLine. Example code for Sprite conversion can be supplied.
For a pixel type of 7, RGB data is provided in RGBRGBRGB... format, making it equivalent to that of CompressJPEG_WriteLine. In this mode, the other flags have no effect.
This extended form of WriteLine requires a greater storage space than that of the standard operation. In addition to the normal storage space required :

item.p: width*3 extra bytes are required for colour JPEGs
width extra bytes are required for monochrome JPEGs

swi-definition.name: CompressJPEG_Comment
swi-definition.description: Add a comment to a JPEG being created

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Data is a string, ignore length and use control termination (10 and 9 are accepted as non-control characters) Reserved, must be 0
Length of comment data (if R1 bit 0 clear)

use.p: This SWI can be used to add a comment to a JPEG in the process of being created. It should be used immediately after CompressJPEG_Start. Comment data may contain multiple lines and/or binary data (although this is discouraged).

swi-definition.name: CompressJPEG_Transcode
swi-definition.description: Convert a JPEG from one form to another

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Generate a progressive JPEG, described by R7 Operation on 'unknown elements':
Copy no additional elements Copy comments Undefined Copy all elements
Transformation type:
No transformation Flip horizontally Flip vertically Rotate 90 degrees clockwise Rotate 180 degrees Rotate 90 degrees anticlockwise Transpose (rotate 90 degrees clockwise + flip horizontally) Transverse transpose (rotate 90 degrees anticlockwise + flip vertically) Reserved
Trim the edges of the output transform Generate greyscale output Optimise for a smaller image
Pointer to workspace, or 0 to read the length

Pointer to scan description block, or 0 for simple progressive (if R0 bit 0 set):
Number of scans present For each scan (repeated), the scan description:
Components within scan Component indices Spectral selection start (Ss) Spectral selection end (Se) Approximation high value (Ah) Approximation low value (Al)

use.p: This SWI is used to transcode a JPEG - that is, convert a JPEG in one form to another form. The most common use for this call is to convert a multi-pass JPEG into a single-pass JPEG suitable for rendering with the built in renderer. For more details about the scan description block, consult the Independent JPEG Groups JPEG library version 6b document 'Experts'.

section.title: Error Messages
section.p: Errors use the error base &8183C0 for the core errors, but some errors use a base of &81A8C0 :

p.fixme: The error base for the JPEG-specific errors is given here as &81A8C0, but the table of those errors is relative to &81A880; the correct base needs to be confirmed.

value-table.value: Bad number of bits per pixel passed to CompressJPEG. The pixel depth of the line is not understood by this version of the CompressJPEG module.
Bad number of lines passed to CompressJPEG. Too many lines have been passed to the CompressJPEG module.
Bad buffer or workspace block. Buffers or workspace is not aligned correctly, they overlap, or their lengths are too small.
Bad width or height. Width or height are invalid for this version of CompressJPEG.

section.p: The JPEG-specific errors have the number &81A880+n. Not all of these are possible with the current version of the module.
